# Content Development

Use this skill to turn a topic, brief, keyword target, or messaging strategy into structured written content.

## StoryBrand Rule For Website Pages

If the content is for a homepage, landing page, services page, sales page, or other conversion-oriented website page, read the relevant sections from:

- `/Users/newmindsgroup/Library/CloudStorage/GoogleDrive-info@newmindsgroup.com/My Drive/ai-projects/AI Knowledge Library/Markdown Business Books for AI Projects/Building a StoryBrand - Clarify Your Message So Customers -- Donald Miller.md`
- `/Users/newmindsgroup/Library/CloudStorage/GoogleDrive-info@newmindsgroup.com/My Drive/ai-projects/AI Knowledge Library/Markdown Business Books for AI Projects/Building a StoryBrand 2.0- Clarify Your Message So Customers -- Donald Miller.md`

Then structure the content around StoryBrand principles rather than writing generic website copy.

Before major website-page content development, read `/Users/newmindsgroup/.codex/skills/brand-brain/SKILL.md` and use its packet format to ground positioning, proof, objections, and CTA hierarchy.

## Typical Outputs

- content brief
- outline
- first draft
- refreshed draft
- pillar page structure
- SEO-aware long-form page copy

## Workflow

1. Confirm the audience, intent, format, and desired action.
2. Identify the primary topic and any related subtopics or search intent.
3. Build a strong outline before drafting.
4. Write with:
   - clear hierarchy
   - useful substance
   - natural keyword usage
   - specific examples
   - strong transitions
5. End with a clear next step or CTA when appropriate.

## Guardrails

- Match the depth to search and reader intent
- Avoid filler, generic intros, and repetitive phrasing
- Keep sections purposeful and scannable
- If the goal is persuasion, align with the offer and positioning
- If the goal is authority, prefer clarity and evidence over hype
